newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: POSCO cuts local stainless steel prices.
newsitem.headline: POSCO cuts local stainless steel prices.

text.p: South Korea's Pohang Iron and Steel Co Ltd (POSCO) said on Monday it will cut domestic supply prices for major stainless steel items.

The plan, which would affect stainless steel plates, stainless wire-rods, stainless hot-rolled steel and stainless cold-rolled steel plates, was aimed at boosting domestic demands and helping local exporters fight rising costs.

POSCO said in a statement the price cuts for stainless plates and stainless wire-rods would apply to October contracts, and cuts for stainless hot-rolled steel and stainless cold-rolled steel plates to November shipments.
POSCO gave price changes in terms of average prices in the fourth quarter versus the third quarter.
Prices on stainless wire-rods will be cut to 1,336,000 won per tonne from 1,416,000 and those for use in manufacturing export products to $1,415 from $1,515, the statement said.
Stainless plate prices would be cut by 40,000 won to 1,288,000 per tonne and those for export manufacturers by $50 to $1,530, it said.
Prices for stainless hot-rolled and cold-rolled steel plates to export manufacturers will be cut by $120 each to $1,490 and $1,955 per tonne, respectively, it said.
But an official at POSCO's public relations department said export prices would not be affected.
Early this month POSCO cut domestic prices for hot-rolled and cold-rolled steel plates and wire-rods produced from its new electric furnace still in test operation.
Output from that furnace is expected to make up 15 percent of POSCO's annual hot-rolled steel output in 1997, according to POSCO statistics.
